edo_map_1670s_80s.title: Edo ōezu, eiri (江戸大絵図, 絵入)
edo_map_1670s_80s.date: 1676 (LoC date; created_published reads 'Enpō 6 [1678]'; Tokyo Univ. identical map dated Enpō 5 = 1677)
edo_map_1670s_80s.description: Manuscript map in watercolor, hand colored, wood block print. Covers Edo Castle and the surrounding area. Oriented with north to the right. Cadastral map showing landowners. Scale approximately 1:10,000. 1 map on 2 sheets, 134 x 149 cm.

ansei_kaisei_oedo_oezu_1859.notes: Originally published Genroku 9 [1696], revised Bunsei 5 [1822], reprinted Tenpō 14 [1843]. Cadastral; north to the right; 117 x 131 cm; includes day-by-day listing of events in Edo for 1859.

meireki_fire_1657.dates: Meireki 3, 1st month 18th–20th day = 2–4 March 1657 (ja.wikipedia); en.wikipedia: began 2 March 1657
meireki_fire_1657.origin: Honmyō-ji (本妙寺), Maruyama, Hongō (本郷丸山)

outbreaks.spread: to Kanda and Kyōbashi, and across the Sumida; ~10,000 died at Reigan-ji and 20,000+ at Asakusa gate

outbreaks.place: Koishikawa: below the front gate of Denzū-in (伝通院表門下), at the quarters of an Ōban yoriki in Shintakajō-chō (新鷹匠町)
outbreaks.spread: Iidabashi to Kudan; most of Edo Castle including the keep burned
south-east to the Shinbashi shore, where it died out

source_quotes: ja.wikipedia 明暦の大火 §経過: '1月18日未の刻（14時ごろ）、本郷丸山の本妙寺より出火 … 1月19日巳の刻（10時ごろ）、小石川伝通院表門下、新鷹匠町の大番衆与力の宿所より出火 … 1月19日申の刻（16時ごろ）、麹町5丁目の在家より出火'

en.wikipedia Great Fire of Meireki, map caption: 'the initial March 2 fire at Honmyo-ji Temple (①), the fire at the gate of the Dentsu-in Temple (②), and the fire in Kōjimachi (③)'; text: 'The fire began ... in Edo's Hongō district'
meireki_fire_1657.honmyoji_note: Wikidata has no coordinate for Honmyō-ji's original Hongō Maruyama site. Wikidata Q11520109 (本妙寺, 豊島区) P625 = 35.739658, 139.735108 is the temple's CURRENT site at Sugamo 5-35-6, Toshima (ja.wikipedia infobox gives the same address); do not use it as the 1657 origin point. (Wikidata Q3140143, linked from en.wiki 'Honmyō-ji', is the Kumamoto temple – unrelated.)
